spec: KILNMOUTH v0.1.1 (design repo, private; D1820-D1849 settled Wed Nov 4, 2026): Claybank Road and the town of Kilnmouth.
_about: Ours, not a design copy. Claybank Road (km_road, the east branch from the fork), the town (kilnmouth) and its six rooms; Route 4's east warps; the holders, scenes and wild tables of Act 2's builds 2 and 3 (the road and the town; Kilnmouth round 1). Map chars are local to the km_town and km_road skins (sprites.js), so the packet blockout is the grid. Named zzzzz so it applies after route4 and Brightgate.

_placeholders.note: PLACEHOLDER copy (Story to replace; KILNMOUTH §4-§6, CABINET §3.5, WALK_BESIDE §4.2, ACT2_BEAT_SHEET B4). Every line, sign, holder name, role name and map label in this file is a placeholder unless a settled packet wrote it.

objs.text: KILNMOUTH, up the clay valley. Springs, kilns and a warm welcome.
CLAY PITS. Mind the little jugs.
THE FORD. Something bobs in the shallows.

lines.else: KILNMOUTH 1. Up the valley, over the bridge.
A water-hammer, stopped. Hasn't struck since the rain quit the hill.
Mud to the ankle. The storm came down here, not up the hill.

objs.deny: The kiln's cold. No fuel vote, no fire.
Night shift only. The gate shuts at dusk.
A note on the door: RELOCATED, WITH THANKS. Have a bright day!
Post's manned. Ask the man outside.

deny.story.km_council & story.km_curfew=back: A card on the door: MOVED AWAY.

lines.else: A bench under the lantern. The lamp is lit even by day.
Crates of ware under a striped awning: jugs, crocks, a few chipped seconds.

objs.text: KILNMOUTH. Mind the runnels. Mind the kilns.

lines.else: A wooden runnel, crusted white. It has not carried warm water in a while.

lines.story.km_springs=warm & story.km_settled: A painted gauge. Each notch is dated in neat brush strokes. The water has climbed a notch.
lines.else: A painted gauge. Each notch is dated in neat brush strokes. The water sits below them all.
A dry ring of stone round the water, white with old salt. It used to be under.

lines.story.km_seat_filled & !story.km_council: BY ORDER. NO GATHERING AFTER DARK.
lines.else: The springs gate. It stands open; there is nothing to keep in.
A grey tower on the common. It hums so low you feel it more than hear it.

lines.story.km_permit_seen: BY PERMIT OF HIGH CHARITY. Issued in default of the council.
lines.else: Hard hats only past the fence.

objs.text: Hard hats only past the fence.
NORTH ROAD. Closed past the hill.

lines.else: NORTH ROAD. Closed past the hill.
NORTH ROAD. Closed past the hill.
NORTH ROAD. Closed past the hill.
One kiln of three is warm. The other two have soot on cold brick.
A fire-bird in kiln tiles, mid-flight. Nobody agrees how it ends.
Ware seconds: a jug with a nicked lip, a crock with a crooked lid.
Woollens. Every hat on the table is a child's size.
Coal and kindling. Coal's dear. Everyone's heating water by hand.
An empty stall.
An empty stall.
An iron grate in the paving. Cold now. The old folk say it used to breathe warm.

objs.text: WORKS YARD: BY PERMIT. HARD HATS ONLY.
BY ORDER. NO GATHERING AFTER DARK.

lines.story.km_council: LANTERN COACH. The coach stops here for Hearthmoor.
lines.else: LANTERN COACH. No coaches till the council sits.
A basket with a wine ribbon. Nobody has opened it.

lines.story.km_seat_filled & !story.km_council: BY ORDER. NO GATHERING AFTER DARK.
lines.else: The council board. Old notices, curling at the corners.

lines.story.km_permit_seen: First one's in Brightgate. Never switched on. Ask them why ours was.
lines.story.km_pitch_f: I grew up in that bathhouse. Give me the seat and the works will heat it again. Warm by spring.
lines.else: I grew up in that bathhouse.
Years in the watch. This town needs order before it needs warm water.

lines.story.km_ask_yard: Ask who keeps the springs clean when nobody pays them. That's who I'd vote for.
lines.else: One kiln of three is warm. The other two have soot on cold brick.

lines.story.km_ask_market: The Bathkeeper. Kept the water warm for years and never asked a thing back.
lines.else: Coal's dear. Everyone's heating water by hand.

lines.story.km_ask_springs: If the town could vote tonight, it'd be the Bathkeeper. It can't. Curfew.
lines.else: It used to be under, that white ring. Mind the frost.

lines.story.km_storm: No storm again! The tower's the best thing that ever happened here.
lines.else: Coats on in a spa town. Gran says that never used to happen.
Hard hats only past the fence.
Go on, then. Mind the tower. It doesn't like visitors.
Curfew, Cadet. No gathering after dark.
Curfew, Cadet. No gathering after dark.
Coal sacks, stamped with the works mark.
A Keeper pennant on the post.
Kilnmouth sits its own seat. The Keepers walk its lanes.
Kilnmouth sits its own seat. The Keepers walk its lanes.
Both sides wait at the springs.

A lamp by the door, turned low.

objs.text: A note by the door: "Rest the whole party. 5 Acorns, or what you have. Kilnmouth"

lines.else: Ware and the usual. Mind the seconds bin, the edges are sharp.
A bin of chipped seconds. Half price, and still good for soup.
Kiln tiles: a fire-bird over the water. The glaze is cracked where the steam used to be.
Notches in red paint, each one dated in a neat hand. The newest is the lowest.
Thirty years I kept that water.
A raised ticket seat. From here you can see the door and the water at once.
A wet-room bench. Dry as a bone.

lines.story.km_arrived: The seventh chair's been empty since the tower went up. Ask anyone why. Then ask me again.
lines.else: Six chairs sit. Six hands. Every vote ends three and three, and the capital signs the rest.
6 OF 7.
The minute book, shelved. Nobody is reading it today.
A stone door, warm to the touch. It opens for a Seal 5 holder.
The firebox. Cold.
The firebox, roaring.
The Hall Stone, warm as a hearth.
The stone was warm before the town was.

lines.intro: Mind the pits. The clay's good this year. The water to wash it isn't.
lines.win: Good hands, {player}. You could dig, you know.
lines.lose: Back to the pits. Mind your step.

lines.intro: You can walk the ford dry-shod. My gran never could.
lines.lose: The ford can wait. Catch your breath.

lines.intro: Up to Kilnmouth? Bring a coat. Odd thing to say in a spa town.
lines.win: Well driven, {player}. The gate is just up the hill.
lines.lose: Rest at the Lantern House up top.

lines.intro: Rained all night down here. Not a drop up top. You tell me.
lines.lose: Go and dry off. The road will keep.

lines.intro: Creek's full for once. Don't get used to it.
lines.lose: The creek will be here tomorrow.

lines.intro: The yard is warm by the one kiln. Fancy a match while we stand in it?
lines.lose: Stand by the kiln and warm up.

lines.intro: Cadet or not, that's company ground. Hard hats only.
lines.win: Fine. Go and look. It is only paper.

kr_s1_first: A round slate bird bobs at the edge of the ford. It hunches small, as if the water were cold.
kr_s4_first: A wasp-waisted bug sits on the clay bank with a tiny jug in its arms.

The seventh chair's been empty since the tower went up. Ask anyone why. Then ask me again.
km_ask_yard: Ask who keeps the springs clean when nobody pays them. That's who I'd vote for.
Three people, three ways of saying it. One name.
km_ask_market: The Bathkeeper. Kept the water warm for years and never asked a thing back.

km_pitch_c: Years in the watch. This town needs order before it needs warm water.
km_storm: Dark cloud rolls in over the hills. Kids run for the bathhouse, laughing.
Over the grey tower the cloud goes flat, like a hand pressed it. Not a drop falls.
No storm again! The tower's the best thing that ever happened here.
{pet} turns to the tower before the cloud does. It waits until the sky is still.
km_permit: BY PERMIT OF HIGH CHARITY. Issued in default of the council.
Below the stamp, smaller: FITTED BY THE LAMP WORKS, BRIGHTGATE.
The spring gauge. Another notch down since you came.
The tower's paper says the council never said yes. Nobody here has read it.
What will you do with it?
km_wb_springs: {pet} stops at the foot of the hill path and won't go on.
You stop with it. Up the hill the cloud sits flat, and nothing moves.
